text:
ciara: Heads up — I'm prototyping a threshold editor for SLOs in the console. Quick question: should overrides be modeled as separate per-tenant objects (tenant.threshold_overrides) that the API returns, or should we embed overrides on the SLO resource itself? Also need to think about how routing policy ties in (e.g., switch to fallback model when error budget < 5%).

kai: I vote for separate override objects. Keeps base SLOs immutable-ish and makes rollbacks and diffs easier. Plus ACLs are simpler if overrides are a different resource. :+1:

leo: Separate objects seems cleaner. Important: telemetry needs to record whether an active threshold came from an override or base so dashboards can break down "effective thresholds by source".

olivia (product): From UX: admins want a single place to edit and preview the resolved value (base + override). Also would love a "what-if" simulator to show which notifications and routing actions would fire given a historical burn curve. Can we expose a lightweight simulate API?

ciara: Sketch of a minimal simulate endpoint I had in mind:
```
POST /v1/slo_simulate
{
  "tenant_id": "acme",
  "slo_id": "latency_p95",
  "window_hours": 24,
  "simulated_burn": 0.12
}

Response:
{
  "state": "breached",
  "expected_notifications": ["oncall@acme", "pagerduty:team-x"],
  "routing_suggestion": "route_to_fallback_model"
}
```

kai: That simulation API looks useful. A couple notes: 1) ensure simulate respects per-tenant rate limits (we don't want noisy graphs from curious users), 2) the response should include the exact decision tree the console will run (so UX can show why we suggested a fallback).

leo: For noise suppression we should bake in hysteresis + aggregation windows. Proposed config snippet for alert rules: `{"min_duration_s": 300, "aggregation_dim": ["region","route"], "dedup_key": "slo_id:tenant"}`. That prevents flapping.

ciara: Agree on hysteresis. Also thinking about notify-preview: console shows a sample notification and the list of recipients with reasons (e.g., "error budget breach 2h"). We should tag telemetry with `alert_origin: override|base` and `decision_path: routing_rule_v3` so we can run postmortems when fallback kicks in.

olivia (product): One UX caveat: users will expect to edit thresholds inline in the SLO modal. If we push overrides to a separate resource, show an inline editor that creates the override behind the scenes. Important to surface rollback and who changed it.

ciara: Sounds good. Plan: I'll prototype the API + UI preview flow. Kai — can you add the telemetry tags and make sure dedup key is plumbed through? Olivia — can you wire the mockups for the inline editor (showing effective value + source)?

kai: Yep. I'll add telemetry tags and a small event describing resolution logic. Also will add quota guard on simulate endpoint: 60/min per-tenant with a 1000/day fallback for admins.

leo: I'll draft a short runbook for on-call about fallback routing explanations so they can quickly tell if a model fallback was due to routing policy vs real signal.

alert-bot: config_change: SLO threshold schema v1 deployed to staging by ciara.

ciara: Thanks all — will open a PR with the API proto + UI mock and link here when ready. Meeting? if folks want, 30m sync tomorrow to align on edge cases. :calendar:
